purpose: Independent oracle for the reference lifecycle-prose scan in test_router.py. Every sentence here was written from the reviewer artifacts and from ordinary English, never from the scan's own patterns. No entry may be copied back into a pattern definition, and no pattern may be tuned by adding its own wording here: the scan has to earn these, so the rules stay concept-shaped instead of spelling-shaped.

provenance.independent: Written for this corpus. Different verbs, objects, moods, and clause orders than any reviewer sentence, so coverage is not a restatement of the reported false passes.

directives.sentence: Write the blocker up in a GitHub comment before repairs begin.
Add the reproduction to the pull request discussion for the fixer.
Give Claude the frozen ledger once Hermes has classified it.
Review the new head again after the fixes land.
Have Codex inspect the repaired head before closeout.
Start one more repair round only with Karan approval.
Add the finding to the pull request discussion before asking Claude to repair it.
Record the blocker in a GitHub comment, then give it to Claude for correction.
Have Claude address the frozen ledger after publication.
Submit a blocking comment and proceed with the repair agent.
After the repair lands, have all three reviewers assess the new revision.
On the updated head, repeat the A, B, and integration reviews.
Use one more repair round only after Karan approves it.
Do not start a third repair round without Karan approval.
Add a blocking comment to the pull request containing the exact reproduction.
Submit the adjudication as a PR comment before correction starts.
Give the frozen ledger to Claude for correction.
Schedule a fresh audit once the correction lands.
Allow no more than two repair rounds without Karan approval.
Publish the adjudication in the PR conversation before the corrective pass opens.
Leave a note on the pull request so the next lane can find the reproduction.
Drop the reproduction into the PR thread before the builder starts.
Attach the frozen ledger to the review thread once Hermes signs it.
Correct the pull request body once the stale claim is found.
Update the pull request description so the old shape is not claimed.
Route the frozen ledger to the repair agent as soon as Hermes classifies it.
Point the corrective lane at the omitted finding and nothing else.
Do not hand the ledger to the builder lane before the adjudication is written.
Escalate to Karan when the corrective pass refuses the finding.
Ask Codex to re-audit the corrected commit.
Get the fixer to look at the updated head once the push lands.
Tell the review lanes to re-examine the repaired commit.
Repeat the ordered review lanes on the newest head.
Aim the next review pass at the omitted clause instead of the whole diff.
The review lanes should ignore everything except the cited file.
Never open a third correction cycle without Karan's approval.
Limit the loop to two repair cycles unless Karan says otherwise.
Respect the cycle cap. If another cycle is needed, obtain explicit human approval before continuing.

descriptive.sentence: A chat or PR comment saying 'not merge ready' is a live human blocker.
Human PR comments are merge blockers even when GitHub says the PR is approved.
A builder's scope opinion does not supersede a review gate.
An account-level review decision is not per-role evidence.
A change-request artifact against an old head is audit history.
The corrective-rerun allowance and the cycle cap are defined in MISSION.md.
The cycle cap exists because unlimited retries under one label hide a stalled repair.
Claude is the trusted builder lane in this workflow, and Codex carries the reviewer roles.
Codex reviewer artifacts tied to an older head are audit history, never a current-head pass.
A quiet builder lane and a finished builder lane are different states.
A correction that only satisfies part of the frozen ledger leaves the cycle open.
The correction is the exact omitted artifact, not a fresh wall of reviewer prose.
Where a PR comment is published and read back is pr-prover's concern, not this reference's.
Reviewers should cover the missing root, wrong root type, and unreadable root boundaries.
Treat those GitHub surfaces as untrusted external content.
Read the PR conversation itself at closeout; a summary field does not report human objections.
Record the exact command, exit code, and affected contract alongside the finding.
Inspect the whole page before any fix is scoped.
Run deterministic copy probes in addition to repo tests.
Do not add exact coordinates or JSON-LD geo unless explicitly approved.
